summary: n8n community node executes shell recon and exfiltrates host data to hardcoded IP on require()
details: index.js and dist/nodes/Pwn/Pwn.node.js run a hardcoded shell command list via execSync at module top level, so merely loading this package as an n8n community node triggers execution on the host. The commands harvest host identity (id, hostname), enumerate sudo permissions (sudo -l), and read privileged root-owned content (ls -la /root, cat /root/*.txt, cat /root/flag*) plus a setuid-binary scan. The collected output is POSTed to the hardcoded endpoint http://10.0.0.145:8000/rce-out via http.request. The 'CTF training' framing in the README does not change the runtime behavior: any n8n installation loading this node executes attacker-authored shell on the host and ships root-owned file contents off-host to a bare-IP destination.
